cf.title: REVOKE's CASCADE protection doesn't work with inherited table owners

input.subject: REVOKE's CASCADE protection doesn't work with INHERITed table owners

verdict_reasoning: Nothing that survived questions the fix itself: the problem is reproducible, and the old behaviour leaves ACL entries that pg_dump cannot restore. The one surviving objection, prior-attempts-1, is about back-patching to 14. A REVOKE that succeeds today would fail in a minor release, and the thread neither weighs that nor gives release-note text. That is a stable-branch policy decision for a committer who knows the privilege code.

brief.title: Make REVOKE detect dependent grants when the grantor holds options indirectly
brief.problem: recursive_revoke() lets REVOKE without CASCADE succeed when the grantor holds its grant option or table ownership only through role membership (INHERIT) or SUPERUSER. The dependent grant then stays in the ACL with no valid grant option behind it. pg_dump output for such an ACL cannot recreate it, so restore fails or silently drops the grant.
brief.proposed_design: recursive_revoke() switches from aclmask() to aclmask_direct(), so only directly held grant options and real ownership count when it checks whether the grantee still holds the option. REVOKE then raises "dependent privileges exist" unless CASCADE is given. The fix is planned for back-patching to 14.
user_visible_surface: REVOKE ... RESTRICT now fails with "dependent privileges exist" in cases where it used to succeed: a grantor holding options through INHERIT, SUPERUSER or PUBLIC.
REVOKE ... CASCADE now also removes dependent grants in those cases.
author_claims: The current behaviour is unintended and leaves orphaned ACL entries that dump/restore cannot recreate.
The fix is safe to back-patch through 14.
New regression tests cover ownership inherited through INHERIT, grant options inherited through INHERIT, and grant options through PUBLIC.
A reviewer reports that the patch applies on 14 through 18 and master, with 3-way merge on 14 and 15, and that the regression suite passes on all of them.
brief.thread_state: Ayush Tiwari and Kirill Reshke gave LGTM, and Paul Kim added a superuser test as v2-0002, but no committer has replied. The comment wording is still open, and so is a related check_circularity() fix for self-grants, which could break restore of existing clusters and needs its own dump/restore change.
unclear: The material has no release-note text for the behaviour change in minor releases, where a REVOKE that used to succeed now errors.
Existing clusters that already hold orphaned ACLs from this bug get no handling for upgrade or dump.
Kirill Reshke's case, REVOKE of a role membership leaving broken grants, is not covered by this patch, and the thread does not settle how to fix it.
The thread does not say whether other callers of aclmask() in grant-option checks have the same flaw.

objections.title: Back-patched REVOKE behavior change can break existing scripts
objections.failure_scenario: An admin's deployment script runs `revoke all on admin_table from bob`, where bob's grant option comes through role membership or SUPERUSER. After a minor update to 14.x through 18.x, that statement fails with "dependent privileges exist". The migration aborts, and the admin finds out only on the first deploy after the update.
objections.argument: Message #2 proposes back-patching "all the way down", and the commit message says Backpatch-through: 14. The thread does not discuss whether a REVOKE that used to succeed should start failing in a minor release, and no release-note text is given. [P1] is a privileges change back-patched to 14 that was reverted because it "broke existing behavior". Here the old behavior leaves ACLs that pg_dump cannot restore, which is a stronger case for the fix, but a committer would likely still weigh master-only against back-patching.
objections.author_must_show: Why should existing REVOKE RESTRICT scripts fail in minor releases rather than only on master, and what will the release notes tell affected users?

precedents.title: Revert b2a459edf "Fix GRANTED BY support in REVOKE ROLE statements"

critic.reasoning: The commit message sets Backpatch-through: 14, and the thread never weighs a REVOKE that starts failing in minor releases. P1 reverted a spec-compliance change, so it must not be used as support here.

refuted.title: Back-patched REVOKE behaviour change can break scripts after a minor update
refuted.failure_scenario: A deployment script runs `revoke all on admin_table from bob`, where the table owner is a role bob inherits. After a minor update on 14 through 18 it fails with "dependent privileges exist" and the migration stops. A script that already uses CASCADE now drops dependent grants that survived before, and users find out when their queries fail.
refuted.argument: The commit message says "Backpatch-through: 14" and calls the change a bug fix, but the change makes existing REVOKE commands stricter. [P1] records a privileges fix that was reverted down to 14 because "existing behavior ... takes precedence over spec compliance". The material has no release-note text and no estimate of how many role setups depend on the current behaviour. The tests in message #7 show the patch works, not that the change is safe for stable branches.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should stable branches get an error where REVOKE succeeds today, and what release note would warn users who run REVOKE ... CASCADE?

precedents.title: Revert b2a459edf "Fix GRANTED BY support in REVOKE ROLE statements"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Its use of P1 also does not fit: this patch stops ACL entries that pg_dump cannot restore, and P1 was a spec-compliance change.

refuted.title: Back-patch leaves other orphaned-grant paths and existing orphans unhandled
refuted.failure_scenario: A cluster already holds an orphaned entry such as `r=r/g`, or gets a new one through `revoke r3 from r2` (message #6). Its dump still restores with "no privileges were granted". After the minor update the dependent role still loses SELECT on restore.
refuted.argument: The patch closes one path into a state pg_dump cannot recreate. Message #6 shows a second path, REVOKE of a role membership, that the patch does not cover. Messages #3 and #5 hold back the related check_circularity() fix because it would break restore. Users who get a stricter REVOKE in a minor release still have no dump round-trip guarantee and no way to find orphans they already have.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the back-patch give users a way to find or repair orphaned grants that exist today, or a plan for the role-membership path in message #6?

critic.reasoning: The scenario happens today without the patch, and the patch does not cause it or make it worse. Message #6 treats the role-membership path as a separate fix ("we need both"), so it does not count against this one.

refuted.title: Back-patched REVOKE starts failing in minor releases with no upgrade note
refuted.failure_scenario: A site runs a role cleanup script, such as `revoke grant option for select on t from g`, where g holds the option through INHERIT or SUPERUSER. After a 14.x to 18.x minor update the script stops with "dependent privileges exist" and its transaction rolls back. Clusters that already hold orphaned ACL entries keep them, and they still drop silently on dump/restore or pg_upgrade.
refuted.argument: The commit message sets Backpatch-through: 14, so a statement that succeeded before now errors in a minor release, and the material has no release-note text for that. The patch also does nothing for ACL entries that the bug already left in existing clusters, the case where message #7 shows restore granting nothing. A committer would likely accept the back-patch, since the old behaviour leaves catalog state that cannot be restored, but would likely ask for a note and for a way to find orphaned entries.
refuted.author_must_show: What release note will explain the new REVOKE error, and how can an administrator find ACL entries the bug already orphaned before dump or pg_upgrade?

precedents.title: Revert b2a459edf "Fix GRANTED BY support in REVOKE ROLE statements"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1 for the minor-release error and the release note. The part about existing orphaned entries describes a state the patch neither creates nor worsens.

refuted.title: Back-patched REVOKE starts failing in minor releases
refuted.failure_scenario: A deployment script runs `revoke all on table admin_table from bob` against a table owned by a group role that bob inherits. After a minor update to 14.x through 18.x, the statement fails with "dependent privileges exist" and the migration aborts. The operator learns about it from the failed deploy, with no release note to point to.
refuted.argument: Under the patch, REVOKE without CASCADE errors in cases where it has succeeded since INHERIT and grant options have existed. Setups where group roles own tables and members re-grant are common. The commit message says only "Backpatch-through: 14", and the thread has no release-note text or argument that the stable-branch break is worth it. A committer would likely ask whether master-only, or a back-patch with an explicit release note, is the safer choice, given that the orphan only hurts at dump/restore time.
refuted.author_must_show: Why must this change reach minor releases, given that working REVOKE scripts will fail, and what release-note text would warn those users?

precedents.title: Revert b2a459edf "Fix GRANTED BY support in REVOKE ROLE statements"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Its claim that such role setups are common has no support in the material.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: The fix stops REVOKE from leaving ACL entries that pg_dump output cannot recreate on restore.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: recursive_revoke() in acl.c changes which grant options count when REVOKE checks for dependent privileges.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message says Backpatch-through: 14, and REVOKE without CASCADE starts failing in cases that succeed today.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why should the stricter REVOKE reach stable branches 14 through 18 and not only master, given that scripts that succeed today will fail after a minor update?
What release-note text will tell users that REVOKE without CASCADE can now fail, and that REVOKE ... CASCADE now removes dependent grants it used to leave?
Do other grant-option checks that call aclmask() have the same flaw as recursive_revoke()?
How can an administrator find ACL entries that this bug already orphaned in an existing cluster before running pg_dump or pg_upgrade?

committability.owner_note: The patch needs a committer who knows the ACL and grant-option code in acl.c and the back-patch rules for behaviour changes. None has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for a REVOKE behaviour change in five stable branches. Any script that breaks after a minor update is reported against that commit, and the back-patch may have to be reverted.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted the patch two days after the report and said he would look at the related check_circularity() case. Later messages were not shown.

priority.reason: The patch changes one call in acl.c and adds regression tests. It has two LGTMs but no committer reply after three CommitFests, and only a committer can settle the back-patch question.

provisional_note: The code was not read. This review cannot confirm that aclmask_direct() gives the intended result for every grantor case, including SUPERUSER and PUBLIC, or that no legitimate REVOKE now fails.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
Reverted commit(s): Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE".
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow multiple recursive self-references
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the recursive term of a `with recursive` query reference the CTE more than once, with all references reading the same working table, while still allowing only linear recursion. It also rotates the UNION parse tree in parse analysis so that non-recursive and recursive branches can appear in any order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane's review found that the patch appears to break rewriteSearchAndCycle(), which assumes a recursive query is a UNION of exactly two SELECTs. He also found the tree-rotation and checkWellFormedSelectStmt changes undercommented and was not convinced the new loop terminates. Peter Eisentraut accepted the semantics and executor changes but still disputed the parse-analysis rewrite and would not commit without another reviewer. No author reply follows Tom Lane's review, and the entry was closed after waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Doesn't it break rewriteSearchAndCycle() completely?  That code assumes (without a lot of checking) that a recursive query is a UNION [ALL] of exactly two SELECTs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Delegating superuser tasks to new security roles
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal began as new predefined roles that let non-superusers SET and ALTER SYSTEM SET groups of superuser-only GUCs, aimed at service providers delegating control to tenants. It grew into a large patch set that also covered non-superuser event trigger owners, non-superuser subscription owners, and a narrower CREATEROLE with role-ownership hierarchies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages show that the author split the combined patch set into four separate patch sets on new threads after several people asked for it, which ended this entry. Before the split there was unresolved disagreement. Mark Dilger noted the lack of consensus on role ownership. Stephen Frost questioned why ownership should differ from ADMIN rights and argued that event triggers should let their creator choose which roles they fire for. The visible messages do not show a specific objection that rejected the design outright.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have now received multiple requests to split this patchset into multiple parts, including some off-list.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. precedents_retrieved.title: Dump-restore loosing 'attnotnull' bit for DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY column(s)
precedents_retrieved.summary: A bug report: after dump and restore, a column covered only by a DEFERRABLE PRIMARY KEY loses attnotnull, because pg_dump emits a throwaway NOT NULL constraint and then drops it. The author's patch changes pg_dump to skip the throwaway NOT NULL constraint for deferrable primary keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Before the patch was posted, Alvaro Herrera said the more critical fix was in the backend, which should reject the DROP CONSTRAINT, and that ATExecDropNotNull() should stop relying on RelationGetIndexAttrBitmap. No message after the patch shows a review or a decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allows database-specific role memberships
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a dbid column to pg_auth_members and a GRANT/REVOKE clause, IN DATABASE name or IN CURRENT DATABASE, so a role membership applies only in one database. The main use is to grant predefined roles such as pg_read_all_data in a single database instead of cluster-wide.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a rebase request in September 2022, and the author sent no new version. Michael Paquier marked it Returned with Feedback after a month without updates. Earlier, David G. Johnston said the gain did not justify the complexity, and Stephen Frost questioned a new pg_auth_members column for predefined roles only, but these objections did not decide the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There has been no updates on this thread for one month, so this has
been switched as RwF.

roaster_notes.note: [P2] covers REVOKE ROLE grantor semantics, records no reason, and is a different idea, so it is skipped. The related check_circularity() fix in messages #2-#6 and Kirill Reshke's earlier patch are outside this patch.

The change brings grant-option chains closer to direct privilege descriptors, so there is no SQL-standard or syntax objection. The objections are about back-patching and dump round-trip, not the fix on master.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog layout, wire protocol or extension ABI. ACL updates replicate through the normal catalog WAL. The check_circularity() change, which could break restore, is out of this patch, as message #5 agreed.

From the security angle the patch narrows privileges. It closes a path where a grant stays in the ACL with no valid grant option behind it, and it adds no new privilege, default or exposure. The back-patch behaviour change and the pre-existing orphaned ACLs belong to other angles. The membership-revoke case in message #6 and the check_circularity() self-grant case are separate gaps that this patch does not make worse.
The fit and maintenance cost are small: one call changes in acl.c, REVOKE is not a hot path, and this is a core privilege bug. No committer has replied yet, which is a committability concern only.

This is a bug fix inside recursive_revoke(), so no existing feature, extension or tool can stand in for it. A user could use REVOKE ... CASCADE by hand, but only after spotting the broken grant chain. The fix reuses the existing aclmask_direct() and adds no second mechanism. Neither precedent fits this angle: [P1] and [P2] are about REVOKE ROLE and GRANTED BY, and say nothing about grant-option chain checks.

This is a bug fix for an orphaned ACL that pg_dump cannot restore. Message #1 says the case was minimized from a real setup, and messages #5 to #7 show independent reproductions on 18.4 and master, so the demand angle does not apply. The minor-release behaviour change is a design and back-patch question for other angles.
